notes: Every turn on this page is the chair's except Pichetto's and Morales's; the chair is printed with no surname, as the era's convention has it, and I did not supply one. The two section numbers (17 and 18) are printed centred on their own line above their centred bold titles, and I joined each number to its title in 'headings'. Three points where the page is typographically odd: the dateline prints a double space in '16 de diciembre de  2004'; heading 18 sets the character after 'Criminal N' as a small raised ring rather than the masculine ordinal used elsewhere on the page ('N˚ 7' vs 'Nº 1849'), and I normalised it to 'N° 7' in the heading text; and heading 18's last word, 'Federal', overflows onto a second line that is set flush left instead of centred, so it can read as a stray line rather than part of the title. The blue underlined 'Orden del Día Nº 1849' is a contents link standing where the inserted text of the order would be — no text of the document is actually printed on this page, so there is nothing to attribute to a speaker there. The unlabelled paragraph 'Si no se hace uso de la palabra, se va a votar.' is a run-on of the chair's 'En consideración en general.' turn, not a new turn. The page ends mid-sentence inside Morales's speech.
